title: Tenant migration triggered intermittent 5xx waves — implement tenant soft-quarantine, connection admission shim, and safe KV compaction
creator: Maya Chen
description: During a coordinated tenant migration on 2026-03-04 we observed repeated 5xx/timeouts across the Hosted API. Root cause analysis shows the migration produced a burst of long-running streaming inference sessions that caused (1) KV cache thrashing and compaction races on the inference nodes, (2) connection pool exhaustion at the edge proxies, and (3) tenant retry amplification from client SDKs. Multiple customers reported degraded service: WhimsyDocs (paying), Ledgerly (enterprise), StudyFlow (trial).
impact_summary: Three customer tenants experienced increased 5xx rates and elevated latency for ~90 minutes during the migration window. Some requests were retried by SDKs, amplifying pressure and causing follow-on timeouts for unrelated tenants in shared pools. SLA alerts fired for P50/P95 latency and error-rate thresholds.
reproduction_steps: 1) Simulate migration by launching 250 concurrent long streaming requests from a single tenant against hosted runtime. 2) Force KV cache compaction on nodes by reducing available mem to trigger eviction. 3) Observe edge proxy connection queues and 5xx responses when compaction delays exceed 200ms.
mitigation_steps_taken:
- Applied emergency soft-throttle on the migration job to reduce parallelism by 70% (2026-03-04 18:15 UTC).
- Temporarily increased connection pool size on frontdoor for affected region and enabled prioritized fastpath for paying customers (WhimsyDocs, Ledgerly).
- Issued customer comms with status updates and rollback options.
- Added temporary circuit for long-running streaming requests that returns a graceful degradation header for downstream SDKs to avoid blind retries.
proposed_fix:
1) Tenant soft-quarantine: a tenant-scoped admission controller that limits in-flight concurrent requests (configurable per-tenant) and schedules excess requests with a redis-backed queue and exponential backoff.
2) Connection admission shim in edge proxy that enforces per-tenant inflight caps and emits metrics (tenant_inflight, tenant_requeue).
3) Safe KV compaction: change compactor to incremental background compaction with per-shard locks and bounded work per cycle to avoid long blocking phases that stall inference threads.
4) SDK guidance update: expose 429-like soft-quarantine status code and recommended client retry/hysteresis behavior in SDKs and docs.
implementation_notes:
- Runtime changes in runtime/kvcache_compactor.cc: implement compaction locks + incremental pass.
- Edge changes in frontdoor/connection_admission.py and frontdoor/proxy_metrics.go to track tenant_inflight and emit tenant tags.
- Redis-backed per-tenant queue in infra/tenant_queues service with TTL and backpressure hooks.
- Telemetry: add kvcache_compaction_duration, kvcache_evict_rate, tenant_inflight_gauge.
rollout_plan: 1) Merge behind feature flag and run canary on a single region with non-critical tenants. 2) Enable soft-quarantine at 10% tenant traffic and monitor error-rate regressions for 60m. 3) Ramp to 50% and then full roll when kvcache_compaction_duration 95th < 150ms. 4) Post-rollback plan: revert feature flag and reopen emergency throttle if error-rate > 2% above baseline.
monitoring_playbook:
- Dashboards to watch: tenant_inflight_by_tenant, kvcache_compaction_duration, frontdoor_connection_wait, hosted_5xx_rate.
- Alerts: 5xx rate increase >1.5x baseline for 10m or compaction duration P95 > 250ms.
- Runbook steps: scale down migration, toggle feature flag to off, add per-tenant throttle, update customers with ETA.
qa_plan: Unit tests for compactor lock correctness and bounded compaction work. Integration test that simulates migration on staging with 500 concurrent streams and asserts no compaction stall > 300ms and frontdoor reports tenant_inflight <= configured limit. Canary load test prior to region-wide rollout.
